Here are five interesting facts about axolotl physical characteristics, along with source URLs for further reading:

1. **Transparency**: Axolotls are nearly transparent, except for their eyes, gills, and the tail, which are opaque. This transparency is due to their lack of vertebrae, which would make bones too dense to see through. (*Source: [National Geographic](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/animals/reptiles/facts/axolotl*))

2. **Regenerative Abilities**: Axolotls have remarkable regenerative abilities, particularly in their limbs. They can regrow lost limbs, and some can even regenerate parts of their heart, brain, and spinal cord. (*Source: [Smithsonian Magazine](https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/the-miracle-of-the-axolotl-180976048/*))

3. **Three Hearts**: Axolotls have three hearts: two pump blood to the gills, and one pumps blood to the rest of the body. This unique heart structure allows them to efficiently manage oxygen delivery. (*Source: [Axolotl.org](https://www.axolotl.org/health/heart.html*))

4. **No Vertebrae**: Axolotls lack vertebrae, which makes them unique among vertebrates. Instead, they have a bony tail and a flexible spine. (*Source: [Axolotl.org](https://www.axolotl.org/health/vertebrae.html*))

5. **Sensory Adaptations**: Axolotls have highly sensitive skin and can detect vibrations, which helps them navigate their environment. They also have a unique ability to sense electric fields, which aids in finding prey. (*Source: [Axolotl.org](https://www.axolotl.org/health/sensory.html*))

These facts highlight the fascinating physical characteristics of axolotls, showcasing their unique adaptations and abilities.
